newsitem.title: UK: Unit trust firms pin hope on voluntary code - paper.
newsitem.headline: Unit trust firms pin hope on voluntary code - paper.

text.p: The unit trust industry will publish a voluntary code of conduct in the coming week to escape stringent rule changes or legislation in the wake of the Morgan Grenfell scandal, the Sunday Telegraph newspaper reported.
The new code will be unvweiled on Monday by the executive committee of the Association of Unit Trusts and Investment funds (Autif), it said.
It will require unit trusts to limit holdings of pre-listed shares to 10 percent of a portfolio. Pre-listed shares are shares in unquoted companies which say they intend to float within one year.
Currently, a fund manager may hold any amount of these shares in a portfolio.
Any manager wanting to break the new 10 percent rule would have to disclose the position within one week, the paper said.

The move was said to be an attempt to prevent tougher unilateral laws being imposed on Britain-based unit trusts, which would drive fund management firms to desert London in favour of Luxembourg or Dublin, the Sunday Telegraph said.
